answer.part: rule determination, ties, tokens and Vagabond pawn
answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing with more total warriors plus buildings than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.

answer.part: normal move legality, repeated movement and rivers
answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin or destination or both, and recheck rule for each move. You may move the same pieces repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy as defender; ruling is not required. Defender may play a matching ambush (bird wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's card is discarded; if foiled it deals no hits, otherwise it immediately deals two hits, not capped by defending warriors, then is discarded. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker chooses order if both sides have effects), roll: higher die is attacker's rolled hits, lower is defender's (equal dice give equal results); each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors, except Alliance defending reverses dice and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Resolve after-roll effects, with attacker choosing order if both have effects. Count hits by adding extra hits (uncapped by warriors) and subtracting ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra defenseless hit; Vagabond is defenseless instead when it has no undamaged swords. Each hit removes one opposing piece; the side taking hits chooses removal order but must remove all its warriors before its buildings/tokens, and chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal counted hits; warrior losses do not retroactively change rolled-hit caps. Each enemy building/token removed scores one VP, whoever removes it, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon, and its current clearing must match every icon; its pawn may activate repeatedly in a turn, but every icon still costs a hammer.

answer.ruling: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP.

At the start of your own Birdsong, win if you rule three clearings of the matching mouse, rabbit or fox suit; bird dominance requires ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting a condition earlier does not immediately win.

answer.part: replacement or discard of activated card
answer.ruling: You cannot remove or replace an activated dominance card.
Whenever a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead.

answer.part: taking an available card, especially bird dominance
answer.ruling: During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so the payment must be a bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it.
Remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal three cards to each player.

Cover the four R building slots with ruins. Set the separate map item supply to 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins, using their corresponding spaces. The four R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword are hidden one beneath each ruin only if Vagabond is in the game; shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return them to empty R slots with identities hidden. Without Vagabond, ruins have no hidden items.
Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This order is distinct from turn order.
Only Marquise may place pieces in its clearing; other players may move pieces into it. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a Keep there is no destination for Hospitals.

answer.part: Marquise Daylight order and action allowance
answer.ruling: First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number except Recruit's limit.
One March is up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. Do not interrupt the compound action to spend a bird card or take another action.
Place one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
Spend a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered space. You need the full wood cost, building and legal slot; otherwise you cannot build.

answer.part: Eyrie Birdsong steps and no-roost recovery
answer.ruling: In order: Emergency Orders—if hand empty, draw one; Add to Decree—add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns (no size limit); A New Roost—if no roost is on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all these pieces can be placed.

answer.part: Decree sequence, suit locations, order and Build restrictions
answer.ruling: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Choose card order freely within each column. Birds are wild for each column. Recruit's card suit matches a clearing with a roost, where one warrior is placed at one chosen roost (Charismatic places two). Move matches the origin clearing and requires moving at least one warrior under ordinary path and rule requirements. Battle matches the battle clearing and requires initiating battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build matches the target clearing and requires placing one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil; do not skip that card or continue other columns.

answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none are face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns.

answer.part: map pieces and rest of turn
answer.ruling: Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings. End Daylight and proceed through normal Evening: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five.
answer.evidence: Actions → Eyrie Dynasties, Turmoil and Evening

answer.ruling: When another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one hand card matching the clearing (birds count) to Supporters. A moving group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. Merely battling there does not trigger Outrage unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.part: no matching card and full stack
answer.ruling: If the player has no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; the payment or no-match draw still occurs.

Revolt and Spread Sympathy both occur during Birdsong. Complete all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy; each can be performed any number of times. Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

Choose a sympathetic clearing with no base and matching a base still on your board. Spend two matching supporters (birds wild). Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed, then place the matching base. Place warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, including the revolt clearing, and one warrior in Officers. Resolve maximum possible prompted placements if supply is short; enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

answer.part: Spread Sympathy eligibility, cost, Martial Law and result
answer.ruling: Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map. Spend the matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token (birds wild). Add one matching supporter for Martial Law if the clearing has at least three warriors of one other player. Place the token and score its uncovered space; only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban applies.
Spend a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers. Supporters cannot pay Train.

Organize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there and scores the uncovered VP; it spends no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but token placement must be legal. Take up to your number of officers in Evening operations, in any order and repetition; officers remain on the board and are not consumed.

answer.ruling: Whenever a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.

answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh first counts tea already face up on the Refresh track: flip two exhausted items face up per tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out of a clearing.

In Daylight, exhaust one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction. Ignore rule. You cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest move only to an adjacent clearing. Slip is the special free-boot exception.

answer.part: forest adjacency, Rest and Evening draw
answer.ruling: For Slip, a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path; on Winter the river also divides forests as paths do. If in a forest in Evening, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea, coins and bags move to tracks if able. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.

Exhaust a torch in a ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track and score one VP if an item is taken. Remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

In a matching clearing, choose a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items and put it in play as completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Draw a replacement quest into the public display; no cards are spent.
Exhaust a hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face. Ready tea, coins or bags move to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. On your own turn in battle, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. A hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally gives two VP total (one removal VP plus one Infamy); a hostile warrior gives one Infamy except the first warrior causing Hostile. No Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike.
Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile; Aid can still obtain a crafted item.

Exhaust a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces. Check hostility; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
Vagabond cannot activate the normal dominance win. With four or more players, during own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate dominance to coalition with another player not already in a coalition.

Partner must have the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; choose among ties. Place Vagabond's score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. Vagabond wins if the partner wins, including through dominance.
A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.

Cards override the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rules win. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so an ordinary card does not override it without explicit override.
If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order.

answer.ruling: Each turn proceeds Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Turns pass clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise takes their turn.
For each hit, choose one undamaged item; it goes to the Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit. Ignore excess hits when no undamaged items remain.

answer.part: number of Alliance Evening operations and Recruit procedure
answer.ruling: Take up to your number of officers in operations, in any order and repetition; officers are not consumed. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
answer.evidence: Actions → Woodland Alliance, Evening and operation table

answer.part: Vagabond Daylight action allowance and order
answer.ruling: Vagabond may take any number of Daylight actions in any order, as ready undamaged items permit. No fixed action-type order applies; the same action type may be repeated as its costs and requirements allow.

Exhaust one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces. A crossbow must be face up and undamaged to exhaust for the action; exhausted or damaged copies cannot pay.
